proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged a finite-sample honest interval upper bound, matching pointwise lower bounds on the interior binary class, and a mixed-rate Gaussian-plus-product limit. The D0.5 referee found the package below the field score threshold; a narrow post-halt repair added missing sampling dependencies and corrected prose scope, and a read-only mathematical recheck passed. The exact local minimax constant, a practical optimizer implementation, and broader-class upper bounds remain open.
tldr: When a binary confounder is reviewed on a scarce public phase-two sample, the overlap-effect correction is a product of two confounding links. One certified confidence-polytope projection is finite-sample honest for arbitrary public intensities \(\lambda_s\in(0,n]\) and has expected length \(\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+(|a|+|d|)/\sqrt M+M^{-1}\}\). At evaluation laws \(p\in\mathcal P_{2\eta}\) and under bounded design ratios, this rate is pointwise optimal and cohort-scale precision has the necessary-and-sufficient binary-model budget \(\sqrt n+n(|a|+|d|)^2\). Only the converse, including the \(\sqrt n\) floor, transfers to larger sparse outcome-dependent-sampling classes containing the binary submodel. The discharged mixed-rate analysis gives the block-orthogonal Gaussian experiment and Gaussian-plus-product transition at \(m\asymp\sqrt n\).
gap: Published two-phase weighted-effect theory assumes phase-two probabilities bounded away from zero, whereas general first-order-degeneracy theory does not determine finite-sample honest length in a public sparse-validation experiment.
fill: The project pairs one computable confidence-polytope interval with a matching pointwise lower bound, derives the resulting chart-review budget frontier, and supplies the mixed-rate experiment that governs the transition.
